history.heading: Taíno and Spanish Jamaica
paragraphs: Jamaica was inhabited by the Taíno, who called it Xaymaca, "land of wood and water". Columbus arrived in 1494, and Spain colonised the island from 1509. The Taíno population was largely wiped out.

history.heading: British colony and slavery
paragraphs: England captured Jamaica in 1655. Port Royal became a notorious pirate haven until an earthquake destroyed it in 1692. Jamaica became Britain's most profitable sugar colony, worked by hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans.

Maroons, communities of escaped slaves in the mountains, fought the British and won treaties of autonomy in 1739. Sam Sharpe's Christmas Rebellion of 1831–32 helped push Britain to abolish slavery in 1834. The Morant Bay Rebellion of 1865 was brutally suppressed.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: Labour unrest in 1938 led to the founding of trade unions and political parties by Alexander Bustamante and Norman Manley. Jamaica became independent on 6 August 1962. Politics was dominated by the Jamaica Labour Party and the People's National Party, and political violence was severe in the 1970s and 1980s. Marcus Garvey, a Jamaican Pan-Africanist leader, is a national hero. Hurricane Melissa, one of the strongest Atlantic hurricanes on record, struck the island in October 2025.

culture.heading: Music and religion
paragraphs: Jamaica has had an enormous cultural influence. It gave the world ska, rocksteady, reggae and dancehall; Bob Marley is one of the most famous musicians in history, and reggae is recognised by UNESCO. Jamaican sound system culture influenced the birth of hip hop.
English is official, and Jamaican Patois is widely spoken. Most Jamaicans are Christian, and the Rastafari movement, which reveres Haile Selassie, originated there in the 1930s.

culture.heading: Food and sport
paragraphs: Jamaican food includes jerk chicken and pork, ackee and saltfish (the national dish), patties and curry goat, along with Blue Mountain coffee and rum. Jamaica is a sprinting superpower: Usain Bolt, Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce and Elaine Thompson-Herah are among the greatest sprinters ever. Cricket and football are also popular, and the Jamaican bobsled team became famous in 1988.

politics.heading: Parliamentary democracy
paragraphs: Jamaica is a parliamentary democracy and a Commonwealth realm with the British monarch represented by a governor-general. The prime minister leads the government. The JLP and PNP alternate in power; the JLP won a third consecutive term in 2025. The government has announced plans to become a republic. Crime, especially gang violence, is a major issue, though murders have fallen.

economy.heading: Tourism and remittances
paragraphs: Tourism is the leading industry, followed by remittances, bauxite and alumina mining, and agriculture (sugar, bananas, coffee). Business process outsourcing has grown.
After decades of high debt, Jamaica carried out successful reforms in the 2010s, sharply reducing public debt. The currency is the Jamaican dollar.
